questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Consider the first ionisation enthalpies of second-period elements. Statement I: The first ionisation enthalpy of B is lower than that of Be because the electron removed from B is a higher-energy 2p electron, whereas Be loses a 2s electron from a filled 2s subshell. Statement II: The first ionisation enthalpy of O is lower than that of N because O has one paired 2p electron, while N has the extra stability of a half-filled \(2p^{3}\) configuration.
options: Statement I is true and Statement II is false
Statement I is false and Statement II is true
questions.solution: Be has a filled \(2s^{2}\) subshell, while B begins 2p filling; the 2p electron is easier to remove, so Statement I is true. N has half-filled \(2p^{3}\), whereas O has a paired 2p electron whose repulsion makes removal easier, so Statement II is also true. Thus both familiar second-period anomalies are correctly explained.

questions.solution: The mixture contains 1.00 mol FeC2O4 and 0.50 mol Fe2(C2O4)3. One mole FeC2O4 releases 3 mol e-; One mole Fe2(C2O4)3 releases 6 mol e-. Total electrons released are 1.00 × 3 + 0.50 × 6 = 6.00 mol e⁻. Acidic \(MnO4^{–}\) accepts 5 mol \(e^{–}\) per mole, so KMnO4 required is 6/5 = 1.20 mol. At 0.500 mol \(L^{-1}\), the required volume is 1.20/0.500 = 2.40 L.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which one of the following property orders is incorrect?
options: Atomic radius: B< Al < Ga < Tl < In
questions.solution: B < Ga < Al < In < Tl The hydration, mobility and spin-only magnetic- moment orders in options 1-3 are consistent with their standard trends.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: The figure shows four 3s/3p valence-orbital arrangements. Which arrangement is the only one that violates the Aufbau principle while still obeying the Pauli exclusion principle and Hund's rule?
questions.solution: In Diagram (1), a 3p electron is present while the lower-energy 3s subshell is not yet filled, so Aufbau is violated. There is no same-orbital Pauli violation, and with only one 3p electron Hund's rule is satisfied automatically. Diagram (3) and (4) instead involve Hund-type issues after 3s is filled, while Diagram (2) is a valid arrangement.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: At a certain temperature the vapour pressure of pure water is 500 mm Hg. A solution made by dissolving 2.50 g of a non-volatile, non- electrolyte solute in 18.0 g of water has a vapour pressure of 480 mm Hg, the molar mass of the solute is
questions.solution: Key Relative lowering of vapour pressure = (500−480)/500 = 0.04 = xsolute. nwater = 18/18 = 1.00 mol. Using xsolute = ns/(ns+1), ns = 0.04/0.96 = 1/24 mol. M = 2.50 ÷ (1/24) = 60 g \(mol^{–1}\).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: The de Broglie wavelength of the electron in a \(Li^{2+}\) ion is 3.324 Å. The electron then de-excites directly to n = 1. The emitted photon strikes a \(He^{+}\) ion in its ground state and ejects its electron. What is the de Broglie wavelength of the emitted photoelectron? −−−− [√54.4 = 7.37]
questions.solution: For a hydrogen-like orbit, λₙ = 2πa₀n/Z ≈ 3.324n/Z Å. Given Li²⁺ has Z = 3 and λ = 3.324 Å, n = 3. Energy of the 3 → 1 photon = 13.6Z²(1 - 1/9) = 13.6 × 9 × 8/9 = 108.8 eV. Ionisation energy of ground-state He⁺ is 13.6 × 2² = 54.4 eV, so photoelectron K.E. = 54.4 eV. Hence λ = 12.27 / \(\frac{−−−−−}{√(54.4)}\) = 1.66 Å.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: A, B and C are hydroxy compounds of three Period-3 elements X, Y and Z, respectively. A gives an acidic aqueous solution, B reacts with both strong acids and strong alkalis, and C gives a strongly alkaline solution. Consider the statements: (i) X, Y and Z must all be metals; (ii) electronegativity can decrease in the order X > Y > Z; (iii) atomic radius can increase in the order X < Y < Z Which set contains only true statements?
questions.solution: An acidic sulfur hydroxy compound, amphoteric Al(OH)₃ and strongly basic NaOH provide a consistent Period-3 assignment. Across that placement, electronegativity decreases from S to Al to Na, while atomic radius increases in the reverse leftward direction. X therefore need not be a metal, so (i) is false and (ii)-(iii) are true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Neutral N₂ and O₂ are each converted into the corresponding monocation by removing one electron from the highest occupied molecular orbital. Which statement is incorrect?
options: Both N₂⁺ and O₂⁺ have bond order 2.5.
Ionization makes N2 paramagnetic and leaves O2 paramagnetic.
Relative to the neutral parent, ionization weakens the N-N bond but strengthens the O-O bond.
The number of unpaired electrons remains unchanged on ionization for both molecules.
questions.solution: Removing a bonding electron from N₂ changes bond order from 3 to 2.5 and creates one unpaired electron. Removing an antibonding π* electron from O₂ changes bond order from 2 to 2.5 and reduces the unpaired-electron count from two to one. Hence only option (4) is incorrect.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: An ion contains 55 protons and carries +1 charge. For this ion, determine (i) the total number of electrons present in all s subshells and (ii) the number of completely filled s subshells.
questions.solution: The species is \(Cs^{+}\) with 54 electrons, having the xenon configuration. Its filled s subshells are \(1s^{2}\), \(2s^{2}\), \(3s^{2}\), \(4s^{2}\) and \(5s^{2}\), giving 5 × 2 = 10 s electrons. All five listed s subshells are completely filled, so the required pair is 10 and 5.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Compared with p-Nitrophenol, o-Nitrophenol is less soluble in water and more readily steam volatile. Which single explanation accounts for both observations most directly?
options: o-Nitrophenol forms intramolecular hydrogen bonding, reducing both intermolecular association and hydrogen bonding with water
o-Nitrophenol forms stronger intermolecular hydrogen-bonded chains than the para isomer
The nitro group in the ortho isomer is nonpolar, whereas it is polar in the para isomer
p-Nitrophenol cannot form hydrogen bonds with itself
questions.solution: In o-nitrophenol, the adjacent –OH and –NO2 groups can form an intramolecular hydrogen bond. This lowers its ability to hydrogen-bond with water and also reduces intermolecular association, explaining lower water solubility and greater steam volatility. p-Nitrophenol instead forms stronger intermolecular hydrogen-bonded association

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Assuming additive volumes, 150 mL of 0.400 mol \(L^{–1}\) H2SO4 is mixed with 250 mL of 0.200 mol \(L^{–1}\) NaOH. What is the normality of the excess acid the final mixture?
questions.solution: Acid equivalents are 0.150 × 0.400 × 2 = 0.120 eq, while base equivalents are 0.250 × 0.200 = 0.050 eq. Excess acid equivalents are therefore 0.120 − 0.050 = 0.070 eq. Final volume is 0.400 L, so excess-acid normality is 0.070/0.400 = 0.175 N.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Consider the central atom in (a) BF3, (b) NH3, (c) PCl3 and (d) BeCl2. For which molecules can the observed number of σ bonds be accounted for by hybridisation without first promoting an electron in the isolated ground-state central atom?
questions.solution: Ground-state N and P each have three unpaired p electrons, so three σ bonds can be formed before any promotion is invoked in this elementary model. Ground-state B has only one unpaired electron and Be has none; promotion is used in the VBT construction before forming three and two equivalent bonds, respectively. Therefore only NH3 and PCl3, meet the condition

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: An element X has the ground-state electronic configuration [Ar] \(3d^{10}\) \(4s^{2}\) \(4p^{3}\). Which option correctly gives its block, period and group?
questions.solution: The highest occupied principal shell is n = 4, so X is in period 4, and the differentiating electrons enter a p subshell, so it is a p-block element. Valence configuration 4s²4p³ corresponds to group 15.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which of the following pairs contain the same total number of atoms? I. 18 g of H₂O and 44 g of CO₂ II. 8 g of CH₄ and 17 g of NH₃ III. 28 g of N₂ and 4 g of He IV. 16 g of O₂ and 23 g of Na
questions.solution: Concept: convert each sample to moles of particles and then multiply by the number of atoms per particle. I: 18 g H2 O = 1 mol H2 O = 3 mol atoms; 44 g CO2 = 1 mol CO2 = 3 mol atoms. II: 8 g CH4 = 0.5 mol × 5 = 2.5 mol atoms; 17 g NH3 = 1 mol × 4 = 4 mol atoms. III: 28 g N2 = 1 mol × 2 = 2 mol atoms; 4 g He = 1 mol atom. IV: 16 g O2 = 0.5 mol × 2 = 1 mol atoms; 23 g Na = 1 mol atom. Therefore only I and IV are equal.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: A gaseous sample contains 0.100 mol of atoms X. The first and second ionisation enthalpies are 500 and 1000 kJ \(mol^{–1}\), respectively; the third is so large that \(X^{3+}\) is not formed. Exactly 90.0 kJ is absorbed with no excitation or kinetic-energy loss. Assume all atoms are first converted to \(X^{+}\) before any remaining energy produces \(X^{2+}\). What is the final mole ratio \(X^{+}\): \(X^{2+}\)?
questions.solution: Singly ionising all 0.100 mol requires 0.100 × 500 = 50.0 kJ, leaving 40.0 kJ. Second ionisation consumes 1000 kJ per mole, so the remaining energy converts 40.0/1000 = 0.0400 mol \(X^{+}\) into \(X^{2+}\). Final amounts are 0.0600 mol \(X^{+}\) and 0.0400 mol \(X^{2+}\), giving ratio 3: 2.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which option correctly gives the oxidation state of carbon in HCN and HNC, respectively, together with the formal charge on carbon in HNC?
questions.solution: In HCN, the H–C bonding pair is assigned to C and the three C–N bonding pairs to N; carbon is assigned two electrons and has oxidation state +2. In HNC, the three C–N bond pairs are assigned to N, but carbon retains its lone pair; it is again assigned two electrons, so its oxidation state is +2. For HNC carbon, F C = 4 − 2 − 3 = − 1, so oxidation state and formal charge must not be confused

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Each option below contains two independent order statements. Select the option for which both statements are correct.
options: Bond angle: Cl2O > H2O > OF2; central-atom lone pairs: XeF2 > XeF4 > XeO3
Bond angle: OF2 > H2O > Cl2O; π-bond strength: 2pπ-3dπ > 2pπ-3pπ > 2pπ-2pπ
Central-atom lone pairs: XeO3 > XeF4 > XeF2; s-character: \(sp^{3}\) > \(sp^{2}\) > sp
π-bond strength: 2pπ-2pπ > 2pπ-3pπ > 2pπ-3dπ; bond angle: H2O > Cl2O > OF2
questions.solution: The bond-angle order Cl₂O > H₂O > OF₂ follows the stated central-atom/electronegativity trend used in this syllabus set. Xe has 3, 2 and 1 lone pairs in XeF₂, XeF₄ and XeO₃, respectively. Therefore both relations in option 1 are correct, while every other option contains at least one reversed order.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: At a fixed temperature, a solution contains 2.0 mol benzene and 3.0 mol toluene. The vapour pressures of pure benzene and pure toluene are 100 Torr and 40 Torr, respectively. Assuming ideal behaviour, the total vapour pressure and mole fraction of benzene in the vapour phase are, respectively
questions.solution: Liquid-phase mole fractions are x(benzene) = 2/(2+3) = 0.4 and x(toluene) = 0.6. P(total) = 0.4(100) + 0.6(40) = 64 Torr. Vapour-phase benzene fraction = p(benzene)/P(total) = 40/64 = 0.625.

questions.solution: Moles AgNO3 = 0.40 × 0.025 = 0.010 mol = moles NaCl in 20 mL, so M(NaCl)=0.010/0.020=0.50 M. For complete ionisation of NaCl, i = 2. With molarity ≈ molality, freezing-point depression = i × Kf × m = 2 × 1.86 × 0.50 = 1.86 °C.

questions.text: How many of the following species contain sulfur in the +6 oxidation state for every sulfur atom present? H2SO4, H2S2O7, H2S2O8, SO2Cl2, H2SO5, H2SO3, H2S2O3 and S2Cl2.
questions.solution: H2SO4, H2S2O7, H2S2O8, SO2Cl2 and H2SO5 each have sulfur at +6; the peroxide oxygens must be counted as −1. H2SO3 has sulfur at +4, H2S2O3 contains inequivalent sulfur atoms rather than all +6, and S2Cl2 does not contain +6 sulfur. Thus exactly five listed species satisfy the condition.

questions.text: A 3.40 g commercial AgNO3 sample is dissolved and treated with 100.0 mL of a KI stock solution, precipitating AgI quantitatively. The excess \(I^{–}\) in the filtrate requires 40.0 mL of 0.100 mol \(L^{–1}\) KIO3 in acid until all iodide is converted to ICl. Separately, a 20.0 mL aliquot of the same KI stock requires 25.0 mL of 0.100 mol \(L^{–1}\) KIO3 under identical conditions. Use the reaction KIO3 + 2KI + 6HCl → 3ICl + KCl + 3H2O and molar mass AgNO3 = 170 g \(mol^{–1}\). What is the mass percentage of AgNO3 in the commercial sample? (Nearest integer)
questions.solution: The 20.0 mL KI aliquot contains 2 × 0.100 × 0.0250 = 0.00500 mol I⁻, so 100.0 mL contains 0.0250 mol I⁻. Residual iodide after AgI precipitation is 2 × 0.100 × 0.0400 = 0.00800 mol, so AgNO3 consumed 0.0250 − 0.00800 = 0.0170 mol I⁻ and thus 0.0170 mol AgNO3. Pure AgNO3 mass is 0.0170 × 170 = 2.89 g, giving purity (2.89/3.40) × 100 = 85.0%.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: The graph shows the vapour-pressure curves of a pure solvent, a 4.0 molal solution of a non- volatile solute X, and a solution prepared by dissolving 5.0 g of a non-volatile non-electrolyte compound Y in 100 g of the same solvent. From the graph, determine the molar mass of Y (in g \(mol^{–1}\)).
questions.solution: From the graph, pure solvent boils at 100 °C and 4.0 molal X solution at 104 °C. Thus Kb = ΔTb/m = 4/4 = 1.0 K kg \(mol^{–1}\). Compound Y solution boils at 101 °C, so its molality is 1.0 mol \(kg^{–1}\). With 0.100 kg solvent, moles Y = 1.0 × 0.100 = 0.100 mol. Molar mass = 5.0/0.100 = 50 g \(mol^{–1}\).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: How many of the following isolated species are linear in their usual ground-state geometry? ICl2–, NO2+, NO2–, SO2, N3–, ClO2–, XeF2, gaseous BeCl2, SF2 and HCN.
questions.solution: Linear species are ICl2– (AX2E3), NO2+, N3–, XeF2 (AX2E3), gaseous BeCl2 and HCN. NO2–, SO2, ClO2– and SF2 are bent because the central atom has nonbonding electron domains or the corresponding resonance/VSEPR arrangement. Therefore the number of linear species is 6

questions.text: All eight letters of the word ABSOLUTE are to be used exactly once. The four consonants must occupy the odd-numbered positions. Among the consonants, B must lie to the left of T with exactly one consonant between them when the odd positions are read from left to right. In addition, among the vowels, A must occur before O. How many arrangements satisfy all the conditions?
questions.solution: The consonants are B, S, L, T, and they must occupy positions 1,3, 5,7. Read these four odd positions from left to right. For B to be left of T with exactly one consonant between them, the pair (B, T ) can occupy only (1,3) or (2,4)among the four consonant slots. Hence there are 2 choices for the locations of B, T, and the remaining consonants S, L can be arranged in 2! ways. Thus consonant arrangements: 2 × 2! = 4. The vowels A, O, U, E occupy the four evenpositions. Exactly half of their 4! arrangements have A before O: 4! = 12. 2 Therefore N = 4 × 12 = 48.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Let n ≥ 2 be an integer. A sequence has 8n + 1 terms. Its first 4n + 1 terms form an A.P. with common difference 2, while its last 4n + 1 terms, beginning with the common junction term, form a G.P. with common ratio 12. The arithmetic mean of the three central terms of the A.P. is equal to twice the geometric mean of the three central terms of the G.P. The first term of the complete sequence is
questions.solution: Let the first term of the complete sequence be a. The A.P. has 4n + 1 terms and common difference 2, so its junction term is J = a + 2 (4n) = a + 8n. The three central terms of the A.P. have middle term at position 2n + 1, namely a + 2 (2n) = a + 4n. Their arithmetic mean is therefore a + 4n. The G.P. has 4n + 1 terms, first term J, and common ratio 1/2. The geometric mean of its three central consecutive terms equals its middle term: 1 2n a+8n J( 2 ) = \(4^{n}\). Given that the A.P. mean equals twice this G.P. mean, a+8n a + 4n = 2 ⋅ \(4^{n}\). Hence \(4^{n}\) (a + 4n) = 2a + 16n, so a (\(4^{n}\) − 2) = 4n (4 − \(4^{n}\)). Therefore 4n(4−\(4^{n}\)) a = \(4^{n} −2\).

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: All letters of the word TRIANGLE are arranged in a row. In how many arrangements do the three vowels occupy positions that form a three-term arithmetic progression with common difference greater than 1, while the letter T occurs before R?
questions.solution: The word TRIANGLE has 8 distinct letters. Its vowels are I, A, E. Their positions must form a three-term A.P. with common difference greater than 1. In positions 1 through 8, the possible common differences are 2 and 3. For d = 2: (1,3, 5), (2,4, 6), (3,5, 7), (4,6, 8), which gives 4 position sets. For d = 3: (1,4, 7), (2,5, 8), which gives 2 more. Thus there are 6 admissible vowel-position sets. The three vowels can be arranged in 3! ways. The five consonants can be arranged in 5! ways, and exactly half of those have T before R. Therefore N = 6 × 3! × 5! = 6 × 6 × 60 = 2160. 2

questions.text: Let α, β be the non-zero real roots of \(ax^{2}\) + bx + c = 0, where a ≠ 0 and c ≠ 0. Define Pk = \(α^{k}\) + \(β^{k}\). It is known that P1, P2, P3 are consecutive terms of a G.P., P1 = 6, and a = 2. Then the value of b + c is

questions.text: Let m be the number of five-digit integers with distinct digits whose first digit is odd, second digit is even, and last digit is divisible by 3. Let n be the corresponding count when the first digit is even and the second is odd. Find m/n.
questions.solution: After fixing the first, second and last digits, the two middle positions can always be filled in 7 × 6 = 42 ways, so this factor cancels in the ratio m/n. Count for First digit odd: 5 choices. Second digit even: 5 choices. Last digit must lie in {0,3, 6,9}. For last digit 0 or 6, one even choice is excluded, giving 5 × 4 = 20 each. For last digit 3 or 9, one odd choice is excluded, giving 4 × 5 = 20 each. Hence the number of admissible triples is 80. Count for The first digit is even but nonzero, so it has choices 2,4, 6,8. • Last digit 0: 4 × 5 = 20. • Last digit 3 or 9: 4 × 4 = 16 each. • Last digit 6: 3 × 5 = 15. Thus 67admissible triples occur. Therefore m = 80. n 67

options: There are exactly 6 possible ordered pairs (r, n).
The largest possible value of n is 12.
The minimum possible first term is 2048.
The sum of all possible values of r is \(\frac{3904}{4096}\).

Given \(\frac{a}{1−r}\) = 4096 and \(\frac{a(1−r^{n} )}{1−r}\) = 4095, we obtain 4096 (1 − \(r^{n} )\) = 4095, so \(r^{n}\) = 1 = \(2^{−12}\). 4096 Since 1/r is an integer, let r = \(2^{−d}.\) Then dn = 12. Thus d can be any positive divisor of 12: 1,2, 3,4, 6,12, which gives exactly 6 ordered pairs (r, n). The maximum n is 12. Also a = 4096 (1 − r),so the minimum first term occurs for the largest r = 1/2: amin = 2048. Finally, the sum of all possible r is 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 3905, 2 4 8 16 64 4096 4096 not 3904/4096. Hence statement (4) is incorrect.
